newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: NZ shares end flat as general malaise continues.
newsitem.headline: NZ shares end flat as general malaise continues.

text.p: * NZ shares end flat, market continues to trade narrow range
* Telecom ends a touch firmer, boosted by share buy-back
* All eyes on RBNZ statement next week
Price movements at close
LAST CHG
137 nil * NZSE-40 cap index +0.78 at 2,288.96
324 -3 * NZSC cap index +8.45 at 5,133.58
362 -1 * Volume NZ$50 million. Futures +2 at 1,138
669 +2 * Other movers - +5 +10
New Zealand shares ended flat on Friday as the general malaise which has seen them trade in a tight range all week continued.
The NZSE-40 Capital closed 0.78 of a point higher at 2,288.96, with market leader Telecom two cents stronger at NZ$6.69.
"It's crept up hugely on the week but in the last couple of day's it's just done nothing," Tim Snedden, broker at ANZ Securities, said of Telecom.

Telecom closed at $6.49 last Friday but shot up to briefly touch $6.80 on Wednesday. Since then it has wallowed in the $6.60s. "That's been symptomatic of the whole market really -- very, very flat indeed," Snedden said.
Telecom goes ex a 9.5 cent dividend on Monday.
Fletcher Building gained 10 cents to close at $4.15, but brokers said it was simply a case of the stock bouncing from recent weakness.

Goodman Fielder was up five at $1.80 after the Australian company reported a A$55.8 million first half profit and said it had reached agreement to buy the New Zealand milling and baking operations of Defiance Mills.

Brokers said there had been solid two-way business in Brierley Investments since it reported its half-year result on Thursday, with 5.47 million shares traded this session. BIL closed unchanged at $1.37.
While the immediate focus for the market was U.S. non-farm payrolls data due out tonight, next week all eyes would be on the Reserve Bank's six-monhtly economic projections on March 13.

Don Turkington at Cavill White said the equity market would continue to tread water while interest rates remained high, and the RBNZ statement had the potential to significantly move both the debt and share markets.
-- Matthew Brockett 64 4 4714 272
